robotsDecisionCensus.whyZeroDisallowedRows: a DISALLOWED page verdict refuses the page BEFORE any request, so it leaves no fetch observation. A ROBOTS_DISALLOWED run is therefore visible as a root that read its policy and made no page attempt, which is how the two such runs were classified - not as an absent row.

theStructuralFindingWorthStatingPlainly.observation: 31 of 99 runs produced zero page evidence, and 29 of those 31 never made a single page attempt: they failed or were refused at the SITE-POLICY step, before any page could be requested.
theStructuralFindingWorthStatingPlainly.isThatACommonCause: NO. It is a common STAGE, not a common cause. The site-policy request is by construction the FIRST request to any host, so any host-level condition - a name that does not resolve, a TLS endpoint that will not negotiate, a connection that is reset - necessarily surfaces there and nowhere else. Attributing those 29 to one defect because they share a stage would be attributing them to the architecture of the first request.
theStructuralFindingWorthStatingPlainly.whatTheCausesActuallyAre: seven distinct mechanisms, spread over 22 distinct registrable domains, nine calendar days and five fetch-policy versions.
theStructuralFindingWorthStatingPlainly.andThisStageHasAlreadyBeenRepairedThreeT: Option B (v2, same-host robots redirect continuation), Option C-lite (v3, same-registrable-domain robots redirect continuation) and the bounded transport retry (v4, robots-only, one token) each addressed a RECOVERABLE sub-case of exactly this stage, each under its own owner decision, and each was revalidated. What remains at this stage is the non-recoverable residue, which is what the next section is about.

viewB.scope: for every one of the 110 selection slots, only the CURRENTLY ACCEPTED acquisition-of-record evidence. Derived by resolving each slot's current occupant from the frozen draw plus the 24-entry reserve replacement ledger, then taking that occupant's latest run in the database.

Exactly one of them - slot 59 - is NOT a canonical success: its formal SD7 range is [1,24], which straddles the threshold of 4, so it is PENDING_CAPABILITY_REVIEW rather than successful. 64 minus that one is the canonical 63.

viewB.theTwoCurrentFailuresDoNotShareAMechanis: one is a TLS endpoint that declined to negotiate a protocol this runtime will accept; the other is an authoritative negative DNS answer. They are different layers, different hosts and different registrable domains.

No CURRENT FAILURE carries a pre-v6 run: both are v6.

howEachCandidateCauseWasTested.verdict: NOT_ESTABLISHED, AND NOT DECIDABLE FROM PERSISTED EVIDENCE
howEachCandidateCauseWasTested.evidence: MIN_HOST_PACING_SECONDS is 1.2 and is pinned by two test files; the pacer is unchanged. It is NOT decidable from the database whether a given pair of requests honoured it, because observed_at is stamped when the observation is PERSISTED - after the response - while pacing is enforced between SLOT GRANTS, before the request, and per-attempt duration is deliberately not persisted. Consequently a same-host observed_at gap below 1.2 s is expected whenever the preceding request itself took longer than the remaining interval, and no observed gap is INCONSISTENT with the policy. This is recorded as a limitation, not as a clean bill of health and not as a defect.
howEachCandidateCauseWasTested.whatWasActuallyMeasured: 2488 same-host consecutive pairs within a run, mean gap 1.877 s, minimum 0.089 s; the minimum was traced to a case where the preceding request's own duration accounts for it.

howEachCandidateCauseWasTested.evidence: 0 pairs of runs have overlapping started_at..finished_at intervals across all 99 runs. Concurrency 1 held throughout the generation.

limitations: This is a DESCRIPTIVE census. It adjudicates nothing, re-opens nothing and changes no verdict, no obligation and no SD7 measurement.

The structural classes in VIEW A were derived here from the database for the purpose of this review. They are not the frozen SD9 taxonomy and must never be cited as per-slot outcomes; the committed adjudications remain the only source of those.

VIEW A's ACQUISITION_SUCCESSFUL class means four or more RAW page-evidence rows. Post-SD7 survivor counts can be lower, which is exactly why slot 59 is pending rather than successful. Raw yield is not a verdict.

Four early 2026-09-21 runs carry no committed run reference under either declared derivation. They are read from the database in VIEW A; none is a current acquisition of record, so VIEW B does not rest on them.
Per-attempt duration is not persisted, so per-host pacing compliance cannot be proved or disproved from the evidence. No observation contradicts it.
Per-run page-attempt accounting is not reconstructible from discovery_method alone. The ceiling was checked against committed assertions instead of re-derived.
Sleep/wake evidence begins at 2026-09-19T17:33:50Z. Seven runs that started earlier are UNDETERMINED, not clean. The pmset log rotates, so no conclusion was drawn from an event count.

Nothing here measures whether the acquisition CAPABILITY could be improved. It measures only whether one common current defect explains the recent low-yield failures. 'No common defect established' is not 'the capability is as good as it could be', and it is not a prediction about the next window.
No statistical threshold, significance test or acceptable-failure percentage was invented, computed or applied.
